detailed_rationale: Supriya Lifescience is a Lote Parshuram (Ratnagiri, Maharashtra)-based API/CRAMS manufacturer with a broad basket across anesthetics, analgesics, antihistamines, anti-hypertensives, vitamins and newer cardiovascular/ADHD molecules, exporting to 90+ countries (exports were 82% of FY26 revenue, Europe alone ~14%). FY26 was a tale of two halves: H1 FY26 was disrupted by repair-and-maintenance downtime at the production facility (Q1 FY26 revenue fell ~9.7% YoY to Rs145 crore, PAT down), while H2 rebounded sharply as Module E at Lote ramped and the base normalized -- Q4 FY26 revenue grew 50.2% YoY to Rs276.5 crore and PAT grew 47% YoY to Rs74.2 crore, with EBITDA margin at 35.3% (vs 36.7% in Q4 FY25, a modest compression despite the volume surge). Full FY26 revenue was Rs827.9 crore (+18.9% YoY) on a full-year PAT of ~Rs209 crore (+11.3% YoY per company disclosures) -- underlying growth is real but the printed Q4 YoY comp is flattered by the soft Q4/H1 FY25 base, so the true run-rate is closer to the full-year 18-19% than the headline 50%. Capacity utilization improved to 74% (from 70% in FY25). FY26 capex was elevated at Rs152 crore (Ambernath facility build-out); management guided FY27 capex back to a maintenance level of Rs40-50 crore, implying the heavy investment phase is largely behind and free cash flow should improve as Ambernath and Patalganga come fully online. Management's own FY27 guidance is ~20% revenue growth with EBITDA margin sustained at 33-35%. On regulatory standing (the single most important pharma-specific risk factor): USFDA inspected the Lote Parshuram API facility Feb 2-6, 2026, issued a Form 483 with just ONE minor observation, and the company subsequently received the Establishment Inspection Report (EIR) with a Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) classification -- a favorable close, no warning letter, and consistent with the site's prior VAI/NAI compliance track record. Balance sheet is close to debt-free (D/E ~0.004x, interest coverage 147x), ROE ~15.9%, ROCE ~22.5% -- capital-light, high-return economics typical of a well-run API franchise, not a distressed or leveraged story. Valuation sits at ~32x TTM earnings (Rs~850/share, market cap ~Rs6,750-6,843 crore, PB ~5.6x), down from a 52-week high of Rs1,085 -- the multiple is full for an API business but not detached from a genuine capacity-driven 18-20% growth algorithm with clean regulatory and balance-sheet optics.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite (final_score_3y 60.0, final_score_1y 56.6, both High coverage, GREEN balance-sheet/liquidity flags) reads Hold on both windows and Hold overall -- under the V1 asymmetric-override rule a quant Hold cannot be flipped to Sell by analyst discretion. Fundamentally I would not have pushed for a Sell independently either: FY26 delivered real (if base-effect-assisted in Q4) growth, margins held in the mid-30s, the balance sheet is pristine, and the Feb-2026 USFDA inspection closed cleanly (1 minor observation, VAI, no warning letter) -- removing the single biggest tail-risk overhang a pharma API name carries. The counter-case is valuation (32x trailing PE, 5.6x book for a ~16% ROE business) and the demonstrated operational fragility already seen once this year (Q1 FY26 production-disruption-driven revenue decline) -- neither rises to the escalation bar of a genuine analytical coin-flip; they are ordinary Hold-supporting considerations, so Hold stands and I have not flagged escalation.
summary: Supriya Lifescience is a debt-free, high-return API exporter that had a bumpy first half of FY26 (a production-facility repair outage) but closed the year strongly as new capacity ramped, finishing FY26 with 18.9% revenue growth and management guiding another ~20% for FY27. Its key US regulatory inspection in February 2026 closed cleanly with only one minor observation and a favorable compliance classification, removing a major pharma-specific risk. The stock trades at a full ~32x earnings multiple for that growth, so we rate it a Hold -- a genuinely well-run, clean-balance-sheet business, but priced for continued flawless execution rather than offering a discount.
positive_para: A near-debt-free API/CRAMS exporter (D/E 0.004x, interest coverage 147x) with ROE ~16% and ROCE ~22.5%, exporting to 90+ countries with regulated-market exposure (US/EU/Japan) underwritten by a clean, repeat-verified USFDA compliance record at its lead Lote Parshuram site (VAI outcome again in Feb-2026, prior VAI/NAI history). Capacity utilization is still climbing (74% in FY26 from 70%), with Ambernath and Patalganga facilities coming fully online and FY27 capex reverting to a Rs40-50 crore maintenance run-rate after a Rs152 crore FY26 investment cycle -- setting up for improving free cash flow alongside management's guided ~20% top-line growth and 33-35% EBITDA margins. New product traction in cardiovascular and ADHD categories diversifies the base beyond legacy anesthetic/antihistamine APIs.
negative_para: The headline Q4 FY26 growth (revenue +50%, PAT +47%) is significantly flattered by an easy base -- Q1 FY26 revenue had fallen ~9.7% YoY on a repair-and-maintenance outage at the production facility, so the underlying run-rate is closer to the full-year 18.9% than the eye-catching quarterly print, and the episode itself is a reminder that single-site-concentration API manufacturers carry real, non-trivial operational-disruption risk that can hit a quarter without warning. EBITDA margin also compressed slightly YoY in Q4 (35.3% vs 36.7%) even as volumes surged, suggesting some pricing/mix give-back alongside the growth. At ~32x trailing earnings and 5.6x book for a ~16% ROE, capital-intensive commodity-API business, the multiple already prices in successful, uninterrupted execution of the Ambernath/Patalganga ramp and the guided 20% growth -- leaving little room for the kind of disruption FY26 itself already demonstrated, and the stock is down materially from its 52-week high, indicating the market has already begun re-rating the growth/quality premium down.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~32x trailing earnings for a business guiding ~20% revenue growth with 33-35% EBITDA margins, the market is pricing roughly a 1.6x PEG -- full but not indefensible given the clean balance sheet (net-cash), regulatory moat (repeat-clean USFDA outcomes across multiple site inspections), and genuine capacity-driven growth runway (Ambernath/Patalganga ramping, utilization still only 74%). The multiple assumes uninterrupted execution; FY26's own H1 production outage shows that assumption is not risk-free. This does not clear the bar for the >=25%/exceptional tier (no ROE/dilution disclosure required), so I am not inflating the estimate to chase the guided number -- I calibrate modestly below management's ~20% guide to reflect single-site execution risk and the fact that the H2 catch-up somewhat flatters recent optics.
